advisory.finding: `rebar.bridge_fsck()` (library) and the MCP `bridge_fsck` tool change from always-returns-a-dict to possibly raising `RebarError(returncode=2)`: `audit_bridge_mappings` now calls `_unknown_event_types_from_ref` / `audit_store_integrity`, which raise `RebarError` on git/ref failure or malformed `bindings.json`, and `_lib_ops.bridge_fsck` no longer catches it, so the MCP `bridge_fsck()` tool (`BridgeFsckOut.model_validate(rebar.bridge_fsck())`) will propagate an exception instead of returning a result. Previously the library/MCP path could not raise on store/scan failure. This is a documented but real behavior shift on a public programmatic surface.
scenarios: An MCP client calling the `bridge_fsck` tool against a repo with a malformed `.bridge_state/bindings.json` or an unavailable git now gets a tool exception rather than an empty/clean result.
A library caller of `rebar.bridge_fsck()` that never wrapped it in try/except now sees RebarError propagate.
